examples.knowledge_point: Computing the Constant Term From the Half-Range Formula
examples.problem:
$$
f(x) \sim \dfrac{a_0}{2} + \sum_{n=1}^\infty a_n \cos(nx)
$$

Let $F(x)=\sin\left(\dfrac{3x}{4}\right)$ for $x\in[0,\pi).$ The Fourier cosine series of the **even** $2\pi$-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is shown above. Find the expression for $a_0.$
examples.worked_solution:
For our Fourier cosine series, the constant term is given by

$$
a_0=\frac{2}{\pi}\int_0^\pi f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $f(x)=\sin\left(\dfrac{3x}{4}\right)$ for $x \in (0,\pi).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{0} & =\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3x}{4})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }{[-\frac{4}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3x}{4})]}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =-\frac{8}{3\pi }(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{4})-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)) \\  & =-\frac{8}{3\pi }(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}-1) \\  & =\frac{4}{3\pi }(\sqrt{2}+2).\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: Let $F(x)={x}^{2}-2x$ for $x\in [0,\pi ),$ and let $f(x)$ be the **even** extension of $F(x)$ to $x\in (-\pi ,\pi ).$ What is $f(x)$ for $x\in (-\pi ,0)?$
feedback.worked_solution:
If $F(x)$ is defined on $x\in [0,\pi ),$ the even extension of $F$ is the function $f$ such that

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}F(x), & x\in [0,\pi ), \\ F(-x), & x\in (-\pi ,0).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, for $x\in (-\pi ,0),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =F(-x) \\  & =(-x)^{2}-2(-x) \\  & ={x}^{2}+2x.\end{aligned}
$$
